name: Preparing Your Home for a Seasonal Roof Inspection

step.name: Step 1: Clear the Perimeter. Before our team arrives, make sure the areas directly around your home are clear. This includes moving patio furniture, decorative items, and any gardening tools that might be in the way. Easy access to all sides of your house helps us set up ladders safely and navigate around the property without obstruction. It also ensures that any falling debris from the roof inspection has a clear landing zone, preventing damage to your belongings.

step.name: Step 2: Secure Pets and Children. For the safety of everyone involved, please ensure that pets are secured indoors or in a fenced area away from the work zone. Similarly, keep children inside and informed that workers will be on the property. This precaution prevents accidents and allows our inspectors to focus on their task without distractions. A safe environment is crucial for a successful inspection.

step.name: Step 3: Provide Access to the Attic (If Applicable). If you have an accessible attic, clearing a path to the entry point is helpful. Our inspectors may need to enter the attic to check for signs of leaks or ventilation issues from the inside. Ensuring easy access means we don't have to spend time moving stored items, allowing for a more efficient and comprehensive internal assessment of your roof's condition. This internal check is key to catching hidden problems.

step.name: Step 4: Inform Us of Known Issues or Concerns. Before the inspection begins, share any specific concerns you have or problems you've noticed. This could include recent leaks, unusual noises, or areas where you suspect damage from a recent storm. Providing this information upfront helps our team target their inspection and pay extra attention to those areas, ensuring no potential issue goes unchecked. Your insights are invaluable for a thorough assessment.

step.name: Step 5: Review Previous Inspection Reports or Warranty Info. If you have any previous roof inspection reports, repair records, or warranty documents, have them handy. This information gives our team valuable historical context about your roof, including its age, previous repairs, and maintenance history. Understanding this background helps us provide more accurate recommendations and ensures any new findings are evaluated against your roof's past performance.
